decision.question: Padding
decision.chose: keep the vertical number (0.2em -> 0.3em, close enough to read as the same control) and tighten the sides to 0.6em
decision.why: a `.item` usually sits in a column of other rows, not alone the way a button is; 0.8em of side padding measured visibly loose next to the icon at 400px in an early look
decision.rule: css#1 read the cascading CSS first

decision.question: Is item() a function ui/ exports, or markup-only like badge.js
options: a real exported function, like table/timeline/keys
decision.chose: exported function `ui.item()`, added to ui/ui.js beside table/timeline/keys
decision.why: the bar in ui/page.js is explicit: a function is for logic a user shouldn't have to carry, and item()'s recursion down a tree of children is exactly that loop
decision.rule: ui/page.js's own stated rule, quoted on that page

decision.question: How does expand/collapse work
options: a JS click handler toggling a class (ux/Tree's / ext/files' way)
decision.chose: native <details>/<summary> — the summary IS the row
decision.why: the owner's own words: "could be a summary in detail element that expands kind of automatically"; it also means ui/item needs no behavior class at all, unlike ux/Tree
decision.rule: page skill law 1, less is more

decision.question: href + children together on one item
options: support both (a linked row that also expands)
children wins; href is read only when there are no children
decision.chose: children wins, href ignored when children is set, documented in item.js and readme.md's Watch out
decision.why: a <summary> is not a link, and combining them (nested interactive elements, or a details that navigates away on click) is real complexity with no caller asking for it yet — v1, ASAP

decision.question: core/Item vs ui/item — merge or keep separate
decision.why: core/Item is headless persisted data (runs in node, a wire format, a Saver contract); ui/item is DOM markup with zero state of its own (the browser's <details> holds everything). A persisted tree that wants this look can call ui.item() per node later, the way ux/Tree already wears ui/tree's classes — full reasoning in doc/core-item.md
decision.rule: code#2 a module is a class; every method is a seam (layering, not merging, when two things solve different problems)

study only, leave all four untouched, write the findings down
